notes: Without-skill CLAUDE.md is thoughtful and has bcrypt warning in multiple places, but lacks YAML frontmatter (not machine-parseable), missing AI-agent-specific pitfalls section, and has 'Common Tasks' instead of 'Common Pitfalls for AI Agents'.
The AI Context section in ADRs is the sharpest differentiator — skill produces it 100% of the time, baseline never produces it (0/1 runs).
YAML frontmatter on CLAUDE.md is another clean signal — skill always produces it, baseline never does. This is the machine-parseability layer.
Eval 1 (inline comments) shows the smallest gap (1.0 vs 0.83) — baseline Claude is naturally good at WHY comments. The skill adds value mainly in the explicit 'do not comment these lines' discipline.
Eval 3 (component+CLAUDE.md) shows the largest gap (1.0 vs 0.286) — the structured template and AI-readable layer are where the skill adds the most value.
Both configurations take roughly the same wall-clock time. The skill uses ~3,600 more tokens on average (reading the skill file), a modest overhead given the quality improvement.
Without-skill ADR added sections not in the template (Migration Plan, References) — shows baseline Claude produces structurally richer but schema-divergent output.
